item.title: MAGA-Loving Elon Musk Says He's 'Not MAGA,' Feels 'Foolish' Over Spending $445 Million On Dud Republican Midterm Election Campaigns
item.text:
MAGA-Loving Elon Musk Says He's 'Not MAGA,' Feels 'Foolish' Over Spending $445 Million On Dud Republican Midterm Election Campaigns
Good morning! It's Friday, November 20, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most important stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.
In this morning's edition, Elon Musk knows he blew $500 million on the 2026 midterms, General Motors wants to double the money it makes off the war machine, Japan's largest automakers are banding together to standardize some processes and Mercedes-Benz says some German plants are in jeopardy as work stoppages spread.
If you'd like a recap of the latest auto news sent to your inbox each weekday, you can sign up for Jalopnik's free Morning Shift newsletter here.
1st Gear: Elon knows he set nearly $500 million on fire during the '26 midterm elections
It's no secret that Republicans across the U.S. went through an all-time drubbing during the midterm elections earlier this month, and while there were many losers, perhaps none was as big as Elon Musk. The Tesla CEO and Republican version of George Soros dropped over $445 million during the election cycle in a futile attempt to get his candidates into office. That very much didn't work, and now he has buyers remorse.
In truth, it's possible that the garish sums of money Elon spent on the election may have hurt the candidates he backed more than helped them, providing opponents with easy targets to latch onto. I mean, it's not hard to claim that the guy you're running against is back by Big Money when the world's richest man is bankrolling their campaign.
In any case, Elon really wishes he could turn back time, and he's about to have a hell of a lot more to answer for when it comes to his companies as emboldened Democratic leaders vow to investigate Trump and his buddies. From Bloomberg:
"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," the billionaire said late Wednesday at the New York Times' DealBook Summit. "Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money."
[...]
Musk's political money overwhelmingly went to lost causes. Two super political action committees he funded — America PAC and Texas PAC — spent heavily to back Republican Senate and House candidates who lost, Federal Election Commission filings show. Ken Paxton's unsuccessful bid to win Texas' open Senate seat drew the lion's share of the money, at some $229 million.
Democrats also won major races further down the ballot in Texas, where Musk has built much of his corporate empire. Tesla has a sprawling factory near Austin, SpaceX launches rockets from its coastal hub reincorporated as Starbase, and the two companies plan to jointly build a chip factory called Terafab.
Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has taken issue with departing Governor Greg Abbott agreeing to award $1.7 billion in tax breaks for the Terafab project and singled out other state grants SpaceX has received. She called for an immediate moratorium on data center development during her campaign and accused developers of raising utility rates and depleting water supply.
Musk nevertheless downplayed the likelihood of any conflict with Hinojosa, saying he expects her to be "quite moderate."
"I don't think she's a far-left governor," he said. "Based on everything I've heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas."
[...]
When asked about the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee telling Trump and unspecified corporate actors to lawyer up, Musk said some in the party were being "a little over the top."
[...]
During his appearance over a livestream from China, Musk sought to distance himself from the Make American Great Again movement, describing himself as ideologically moderate. "I'm not MAGA," he said.
Technically, Musk is correct. He's not MAGA. As he told supporters in 2024, he is actually "Dark MAGA."
2nd Gear: GM wants to double what it makes off defense
General Motors wants to expand the money it makes off of wars by more than doubling its defense revenue to $2 billion in the next few years. It looks to take advantage of global defense companies turning to its automotive technology to accelerate their weapons production.
Back in August, GM delivered its first batch of Patriot missile components to Lockheed Martin within 22 days of the two companies entering a partnership in weapons manufacturing — something championed by the Trump administration. Several other large defense companies with governmental ties have also lined up to sign deals with GM. From the Financial Times:
"We have massive manufacturing capabilities to build defence equipment components. We have so many defence companies coming to us and saying help us," Stephen duMont, head of GM Defense, said in an interview in London.
In recent years, companies including Volkswagen, Jaguar Land Rover and Renault have diversified into the defence sector in search of new sources of revenue as profits become squeezed in the traditional automotive business due to cut-throat competition and higher costs.
Jim Farley, Ford's chief executive, confirmed earlier this year that it was also in discussions with the US government on defence-related projects, while Stellantis last week agreed to sell its Brampton plant to Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel and explore "global collaboration".
GM's ties to defence stretch back decades. It played a pivotal part in America's "Arsenal of Democracy" campaign during the second world war, converting all of its US plants to support the war effort. The group sold its defence business in 2003 and later re-established GM Defense as a subsidiary in 2017 after Mary Barra became chief executive.
"Mary recognised from early on the opportunity to leverage GM's investment in the automotive business for profitable growth of the defence business," said duMont, a former Raytheon executive.
The defence unit, a separate subsidiary that now has about 500 to 600 employees, was "like a start-up", allowing for quicker decision-making and operational changes.
In the grand scheme of things (read: General Motors), the defense unit is minuscule. It only generates about $1 billion in revenue every year, which isn't exactly nothing, but when compared with the group's total revenue of $185 billion, it's sort of small potatoes. That's why CEO Mary Barra wants to expand it.
It isn't just parts of weapons, either. It's also vehicles. The U.S. Army recently increased orders for Infantry Squad Vehicles from an initial 649 vehicles to nearly 12,000 — which could lead to a $1 billion contract. In addition, it's looking at getting in on the defense business in Europe and the UK.
The business of war is booming, and GM wants in on the action.
3rd Gear: Japans largest automakers are standardizing components to fight China
Japan's largest automakers, including Toyota, Honda and Nissan, are starting a new initiative to compete less and collaborate more as a way to deal with cheap Chinese competition. The first three things they'll do are harmonize quality criteria for steel, unify recycling protocols for plastics, and create a universal color-coding scheme for wire harnesses, but more steps are on the way. The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association says these and any other big changes are coming to any suppliers doing business with Japanese automakers. From Automotive News:
Discussions will begin with Japanese suppliers but soon encompass international ones.
JAMA Chairman Koji Sato, who is also vice chairman of Toyota Motor Corp., launched the campaign after taking the helm of the industry lobby group in January. Leaders announced an agreement on steel, resin, and wire harnesses at the group's last regular meeting of the year here to set the stage for implementing harmonization from 2027.
The urgent efficiency drive is one of the most ambitious attempts yet to reshape a sprawling supply base spanning Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi and Suzuki. The goal: sharpen Japan Inc.'s edge amid an onslaught of new technologies and cutthroat new competitors from China by cutting costs and channeling the savings into innovation.
"We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change," Sato said. "Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas."
A JAMA task force leading the push has been working all year to formulate a framework. They decided on steel, resin and wire harnesses partly because they are areas of the vehicle that go unnoticed by customers and do not directly impact brand value or differentiation. The areas also account for a large portion of a vehicle's input costs, allowing for a large immediate impact.
JAMA said about 70,000 variants of wire harnesses are a prime candidate for consolidation.

Koenigsegg Is Now Worth $1.4 Billion After New Investment
Christian von Koenigsegg will continue to lead the company’s strategy, innovation, and product vision.
A major financial boost for Koenigsegg has revealed its valuation. The Swedish automaker has secured new investment from a private equity firm, and the deal reportedly values the company at about €1.3 billion ($1.4 billion at today’s exchange rate).
The deal with 65 Equity Partners, a Singapore-based private equity firm that is now a minority shareholder, “will enable Koenigsegg to accelerate its expansion and technology development as well as its business systems,” according to the press release announcing the agreement.
Koenigsegg has grown considerably in recent years, reporting €155 million ($170.4 million) in revenue for 2025. That represents a growth of approximately 80 percent since 2022. Demand continues to outstrip production, with the company employing approximately 800 people worldwide.
Christian Von Koenigsegg
Under the agreement, 65 Equity Partners will invest €20 million in Koenigsegg. It will become a minority shareholder and the company's second institutional investor, according to Bloomberg. Chieftain Capital Management, an existing shareholder, will invest additional money, increasing its ownership stake.
Christian von Koenigsegg, the company's founder and CEO, will remain its majority owner. He will continue to lead the company's strategy, innovation, and product vision. Koenigsegg said of the deal:
‘This partnership gives us additional resources to bring our ambitions to life, while preserving the entrepreneurial spirit and engineering freedom that define Koenigsegg.’
The company’s chief financial officer, Johan Ekdah, told Bloomberg that the deal is “not about raising cash,” adding that the company can fund its own projects. It does create “headroom for the future.”
Koenigsegg Gemera
Koenigsegg has started Gemera production, a four-passenger hypercar first unveiled in 2020. It has 2,300 horsepower and 2,028 pound-feet of torque, and the company plans to produce 300.

This Blacked-Out Bentley Torcal Is Limited To Just 20 Units
Stealth wealth looks best in black
Bentley hasn't even delivered its first Torcal yet, but it's already going on its second limited-edition version of the all-electric SUV. First, there was the aptly named Torcal First Edition, and now the automaker has revealed a new bespoke commission. This blacked-out beast has been crafted by Japanese streetwear designer Hiroshi Fujiwara, and just 20 units will be built. For interested shoppers who are looking for an EV that doesn't shout about being electric, this might be it.
Each will be painted in Beluga black, which pairs well with the black badges, blacked-out grille, and the stunning 22-inch Vortex wheels that, you guessed it, are black. Unlike some EV wheels that have uninspired aero discs designed to improve aerodynamics, these fully forged wheels have carbon fiber inserts that look cool while slicing through the air.
Fujiwara founded Tokyo design label FRGMT in 2003, and this special Torcal features some of the company's branding. Positioned on the front fenders is small Bentley // FRGMT text, and there's also an FRGMT logo on the tailgate.
Just like the exterior, the interior of this Torcal is dark and stealthy, revealing a combination of Imperial Blue and Beluga black trim with cross-stitching and piano black accents. Dozens of small FRGMT and Bentley logos have been added to the SUV's door panels, and there are also unique treadplates for some added Japanese streetwear style.
The Torcal is an all-electric conquerer
Bentley announced that the Torcal is already sold out for the first model year, but it hasn't released much info about this blacked-out special, including which markets will get it, how much it will cost, or if it's based on the standard Torcal or the higher-spec Torcal S. The Bentley Torcal will launch as a 2028 model in the U.S. and start at $222,150, including a hefty $4,150 in destination, title, taxes, and dealer charges.
All versions of the 2028 Bentley Torcal use a 113-kWh battery pack and an 800-volt electrical architecture. The standard model rocks two electric motors with 810 horsepower and 881 pound-feet (1,194 Nm), while the Torcal S lifts these figures to 876 hp and 996 lb-ft (1,350 Nm) during launch control. Despite the EV's size and 2,700 kg (almost 6,000 pounds) curb weight, it needs just 2.8 seconds to hit 60 mph (96 kph), making it quicker than a Porsche 911 GT3 RS off the line.
It's not just the sheer performance on offer that makes the Torcal seem impressive. It supports DC charging speeds of up to 400 kW, meaning the battery can be charged from 10-80% in less than 20 minutes. The quoted driving range of up to 375 miles (600 km) isn't industry-leading, but if you live somewhere with ample fast-charging stations, that shouldn't be a big deal.

item.text:
VW Revives Golf GTI Rabbit Edition In The U.S.
The limited-run hot hatch borrows from the Golf R and Europe’s GTI Edition 50, but skips one key upgrade.
VW has unveiled a special Rabbit Edition for the 2027 Golf GTI in the U.S., reviving a nameplate that was last used in 2019. The limited-edition model comes with several visual and chassis upgrades but has not received any alterations to the engine.
The highlight of the Rabbit Edition is the distinctive Dark Moss Green Metallic paint. It's the same as that found on the Golf GTI Edition 50 sold in Europe. This paint has a beautiful metallic finish with shiny flakes that glisten in the sun, and that's just in these photos. We bet it looks even better in person. The special touches made to the Rabbit Edition don't end with the paint.
It borrows parts from the Golf R Black Edition, like the black VW logos, black grille, and black accents around the headlights. The hot hatch also sits on a set of lovely black 19-inch wheels clad in summer performance tires, has a black roof, and black wing mirrors. The only touch of color on the outside, other than the green paint, is the red brake calipers and the red GTI badges. A small rabbit emblem is positioned on the tailgate. VW has made some minor tweaks to the car's cabin, wrapping the seats in a suede-like material with quilted stitching and red accents.
The engine is the same, but the suspension is better
As mentioned, VW hasn't messed with the car's engine. As such, the familiar turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 EA888 continues to deliver 241 horsepower and 273 pound-feet of torque and is mated to a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission. That's a bit of a shame, as the European GTI Edition 50, from which the Rabbit Edition gets its special paint finish, is significantly more powerful. Its 2.0-liter turbo has been tuned to make 321 hp and 310 lb-ft. If buyers want to make those kinds of figures in America, they'll need to turn to the aftermarket.
There is one key performance change that will help the Rabbit Edition perform better than a base Golf GTI on a track and across a mountain pass. It comes standard with the usually optional DCC adaptive damping system, which reacts to the road and steering inputs to automatically adjust the damping at each corner. These dampers are ordinarily only found on America's Golf GTI Autobahn model.
VW will announce prices for the Golf GTI Rabbit Edition before sales kick off in the second quarter of 2027.

item.title: 2027.5 VW GTI Rabbit Edition Aims for the Goldilocks Spot in the Lineup
item.text:
Mid-year model automobiles are like safeties in football games: rare, but maybe not as uncommon as you might guess at first. But the latest in that tradition, the 2027.5 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition, doesn’t just split the difference between 2027 and 2028; it also slides between the S and SE models that make up the lower tiers of the lineup, while bringing along some of the sweet features from the top-shelf GTI Autobahn trim. In other words, it has the makings of a Goldilocks special.
First, a dash of history. “Rabbit” was the name originally used by VW for the Golf in the U.S. and Canadian markets back in the days of the Mk1, including on the first GTI that arrived in 1979 in the Great White North and in ‘83 in the States. (The company then returned to the Rabbit name for the Mk5 Golf here, but that’s less consequential—or memorable.) In honor of that first GTI, this new trim includes an adorable little chrome bunny on its hatch, in addition to blacked-out mirror caps, grille, and other trim bits scattered around the exterior that replace red items on other members of the current GTI family.
The GTI Rabbit Edition also boasts the first North American use of Dark Moss Green Metallic, a paint job previously reserved for Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 that set the front-wheel drive Nurburgring lap record. The 19-inch black wheels come from the Golf R, and are wrapped as standard in summer performance tires, versus the all-season rubber that normally comes with less-expensive GTIs. But the most notable change on the fun side is the presence of the DCC adaptive dampers, for which you otherwise would have to spring for the top-shelf Autobahn trim to get. Inside, meanwhile, the Rabbit Edition picks up the GTI SE’s GTI Clubsport ArtVelours material on its comfy yet supportive front buckets and rear bench.
Like all other current GTIs, unfortunately, the Rabbit Edition forces buyers to use a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic to change the gears tied to its 241-horsepower turbocharged inline-four; the manual gearbox remains locked in the past. Still, if you can look past that, the Rabbit Edition has the makings of a steal. Volkswagen hasn’t announced pricing yet—that’ll come closer to its on-sale date of Q2 2027—but seeing as how the carmaker is quite explicit about where it lands in the lineup, expect it to come in the $36,250 of the GTI S and the $40,240 of the GTI SE, plus or minus any little price bumps they might pick up in the next half model year.

Totem Automobili has taken another run at the Alfa Romeo GTA and it might be just be the most seductive Italian since Sophia Loren.
With a timeless beauty combined with hypercar power the $1.3 M GTAmodificata takes Alfa’s 105-series to a whole new level.
Modelled on the 1970 and 1971 European Touring Car Championship-winning GTAm built by Autodelta, Totem’s car retains its classic look, complete with exposed rivets, although the monocoque and bodywork is actually all carbon fiber. Aluminum is used for the front and rear subframes to keep weight down to a paltry 1095 kg (2414 lbs), while the 3.2-liter twin-turbo V-6 from Italtecnica delivers 810 hp and 538 lbft of torque. For comparison, the Ferrari SF90 makes 786 hp and weighs almost 1500 lbs more.
The 90-degree V-6 features dry sump lubrication, individual throttle bodies and a 3D-printed stainless steel exhaust manifold. Back in 1971 the GTAm Touring Car produced 240 hp and that was no slouch, but with more than three times the horsepower the Totem GTAmodificata can dispatch 62 mph from a standstill in 2.6 seconds and reach a vMax of 186 mph. This prodigious power is sent to the rear wheels via a six-speed sequential transmission and limited-slip differential.
With 200 horsepower more than the company’s previous GT Super and GT Electric, the GTAmodificata is also lighter, eschewing paint (for the most part) in favor of exposed carbon fiber outside and in. Even the stunning dished wheels, which evoke the classic GTA, use lightweight carbon and aluminum to save weight.
The GTAmodificato marks the end of the line for Totem’s Giulia GT-inspired cars and just five will be made.

Totem Automobili has taken another run at the Alfa Romeo GTA and it might be just be the most seductive Italian since Sophia Loren.
With a timeless beauty combined with hypercar power the $1.3 M GTAmodificata takes Alfa’s 105-series to a whole new level.
Modelled on the 1970 and 1971 European Touring Car Championship-winning GTAm built by Autodelta, Totem’s car retains its classic look, complete with exposed rivets, although the monocoque and bodywork is actually all carbon fiber. Aluminum is used for the front and rear subframes to keep weight down to a paltry 1095 kg (2414 lbs), while the 3.2-liter twin-turbo V-6 from Italtecnica delivers 810 hp and 538 lbft of torque. For comparison, the Ferrari SF90 makes 786 hp and weighs almost 1500 lbs more.
The 90-degree V-6 features dry sump lubrication, individual throttle bodies and a 3D-printed stainless steel exhaust manifold. Back in 1971 the GTAm Touring Car produced 240 hp and that was no slouch, but with more than three times the horsepower the Totem GTAmodificata can dispatch 62 mph from a standstill in 2.6 seconds and reach a vMax of 186 mph. This prodigious power is sent to the rear wheels via a six-speed sequential transmission and limited-slip differential.
With 200 horsepower more than the company’s previous GT Super and GT Electric, the GTAmodificata is also lighter, eschewing paint (for the most part) in favor of exposed carbon fiber outside and in. Even the stunning dished wheels, which evoke the classic GTA, use lightweight carbon and aluminum to save weight.
The GTAmodificato marks the end of the line for Totem’s Giulia GT-inspired cars and just five will be made.

item.title: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Reportedly Standardize Vehicle Parts in Bid to Lower Costs
item.angle: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs
item.text:
- Toyota, Nissan, and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News.
- The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses.
- Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon.
Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.
In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.
The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.
The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.
“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”

item.title: 2027 Toyota Sienna Refreshed to Give the Hybrid Minivan More Efficiency and Power
item.angle: 2027 Toyota Sienna Refreshed to Give the Hybrid Minivan More Efficiency and Power
item.text:
- Toyota’s 2027 Sienna mid-cycle refresh focuses on improvements under the skin.
- A new sixth-gen hybrid system both makes more power and offers better fuel economy.
- Arriving at dealers in early 2027, the revised Sienna is estimated to start around $44,500.
Some mid-cycle updates focus on aesthetics, bringing some new style (and hopefully some new eyes) to a slightly older product. The 2027 Toyota Sienna skipped those pleasantries and focused on the meat and potatoes: its hybrid powertrain.
The 2027 Toyota Sienna looks no different—unless you count the Cypress paint color, which was dropped and swapped with Storm Cloud—but it’s what’s lying under the body that matters more here. The Sienna adopts Toyota’s sixth-generation hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the upscale Lexus ES Hybrid. A new electric motor packs more efficient silicon-carbide conductors, and it pairs with a 1.15-kWh battery that ditches the old nickel-metal hydride chemistry in favor of lithium-ion. In addition, there’s a whole new electrical platform underpinning it all, with new ECUs and software to manage everything.
Combine all that with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine that has been retuned for quieter low-speed operation, and you have a Toyota Sienna that produces a whopping six horsepower more than before, rising from 245 horses to 251. Engine torque is unchanged at 176 pound-feet, and Toyota did not specify e-motor torque. That small power bump is enough to affect its acceleration: Toyota estimates a 7.5-second sprint to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive Sienna variants, rising to 7.6 seconds with AWD. That’s 0.3 or 0.4 second quicker than before, respectively.
Even with that bump in speed, Toyota claims improved fuel economy in the 2027 Sienna, to the tune of +3 mpg in the city for FWD models and +4 mpg in the city for AWD models. Combined estimates rise 1 or 2 mpg. For context, the 2026 model is EPA estimated at 36 mpg city/36 highway/36 combined for the front-driver, and 35/36/35 for the AWD.
There have also been some tweaks to other electrical-adjacent components. The electronic power steering promises less effort at low speeds, while improving on-center feel at highway speeds. That adjustment includes a new steering-wheel layout that will eventually migrate to other sixth-gen-equipped hybrids. Toyota also fiddled with its brake electronics, resulting in less pedal effort and a smoother blend between regen and friction braking. The Sienna also includes something Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels with the aim to reduce body roll during cornering.
Creature comforts get some upgrades as well. A 12.3-inch infotainment screen is now standard across the lineup (the LE grade ditches its 8.0-incher), as is a 12.3-inch gauge cluster (LE and XLE get this instead of the old 7.0-inch getup). There’s new LED cabin lighting, plus a revised rear-seat entertainment system that now features native apps on a new touchscreen. Upgraded dashboard sound abatement promises to lower the cabin volume by one decibel.
Toyota also slimmed down the Sienna’s trims for 2027. The Limited grade has been dropped in favor of adding more features to the sporty XSE variant, which rises to become the trim underneath the Platinum. As a result, the 2027 Sienna XSE picks up niceties like ventilated front seats with memory, a panoramic-view monitor, and a head-up display. The rugged Woodland Edition trim also picks up the surround-view tech. The upgraded rear-seat entertainment is available on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum trims.
The 2027 Toyota Sienna reaches dealerships in early—you guessed it—2027. Pricing starts around $44,500 for the front-wheel-drive LE base trim, which represents a price bump of less than $2000 over a base 2026 Sienna. Not too shabby for a whole new generation of powertrain.

item.title: Ferrari's New 296 Challenge Stradale Is A 670-HP Race Car You Can Drive Home
item.text:
Ferrari's New 296 Challenge Stradale Is A 670-HP Race Car You Can Drive Home
With 670 horsepower, 1,360 pounds of downforce, and a race-car-derived chassis, this is no ordinary road-going Ferrari.
The curtains open, and for a moment, you're completely transfixed. You know right away that you're looking at something special. This car represents a turning point for Ferrari, a significant departure from what came before. It's a genuine race car that's still somehow legal to drive on the street.
"This is a disruption of balance," says one of the people most closely involved in bringing the car to life. It's easy to see what he means. Even standing still, the Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale looks like a car built with one thing in mind: setting lap times.
Ferrari even calls it "the production car with the closest connection to a competition vehicle."
No hybrid system. 670 horsepower. Just 2,932 pounds. And 1,360 pounds of downforce at 155 miles per hour. The car was developed alongside the 296 Challenge Evo, which will compete in Ferrari's one-make racing series starting in 2027. The price? Around $307,000.
Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale
"It's a physical car, fundamentally different to drive. It's not like the 296 Speciale, which is easier and more immediate." Those two sentences tell you almost everything you need to know.
The Speciale is incredibly fast, but it's also approachable. Its electric motor helps with corner exits, drifting, and straight-line acceleration. The Challenge Stradale does away with all of that. There's no hybrid system and no electric motor to fill in the gaps. It's a raw, uncompromising machine with a narrower margin for error, one that relies on aerodynamics to do much of the heavy lifting.
The connection between Ferrari's road cars and its racing program goes back to the company's roots. Enzo Ferrari lived for competition, and in the early days, building road cars was largely a way to fund his racing ambitions. That relationship continues today through the Ferrari Challenge, a customer racing series that has been running since 1993.
It started with the 348, followed by the F355, 360, and every generation since. The 296 Challenge Stradale brings that racing DNA closer to the road than any production Ferrari before it.
Under the hood is the familiar twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 from the 296, with both turbochargers mounted inside the V. The difference is that it now works entirely on its own, producing:
- 670 Horsepower At 8,000 RPM
- 546 Pound-Feet Of Torque At 6,250 RPM
- 8,500-RPM Redline
For comparison, the competition-focused 296 Challenge Evo produces 700 hp.
The turbochargers are carried over from the 296 Challenge, as are the thermal barriers. Ferrari focused its development work on boost pressure, variable valve timing, and insulation. The result is a dynamic torque increase of more than 32 percent compared to the 296 GTB. Without an electric motor smoothing things out, throttle response is also much sharper.
The eight-speed dual-clutch transmission has two distinct personalities. Push the car hard, and it switches to the aggressive shifting logic from the 296 Challenge, delivering gear changes in around 170 milliseconds. At lower speeds, it adopts a smoother calibration borrowed from the SF90 XX Stradale. The exhaust note builds all the way to 8,500 rpm, exiting through twin tailpipes derived from the race car.
Performance is predictably serious. The 296 Challenge Stradale hits 60 mph in 2.8 seconds, reaches 124 mph in 7.9 seconds, and tops out at more than 186 mph. Around Ferrari's Fiorano test track, it completes a lap in 1 minute and 18.5 seconds.
The dry weight is just 2,932 pounds with optional equipment, making it 308 pounds lighter than the 296 GTB. That's also the same figure as the 296 Challenge Evo. The result is a power-to-weight ratio of 4.37 pounds per horsepower.
A big part of the weight savings comes from removing the battery and electric motor. Ferrari also fitted a dedicated transmission with a lighter shaft and casing. Then there's the carbon fiber, which appears throughout the car:
- Rear wing and hood trim: Both use lightweight carbon fiber.
- Door panels: One-piece carbon-fiber construction, without conventional armrests or storage pockets.
- Seats: Carbon-fiber tubular seats that are 25% lighter than standard racing seats.
For the first time on a production Ferrari, buyers can also request removable seat coverings, leaving parts of the underlying structure exposed.
One figure says a lot about how the Challenge Stradale behaves through corners: body roll is down 68 percent compared to the 296 GTB. Lateral performance improves by 7 percent, while stability increases by 34 percent.
The springs are roughly twice as stiff, requiring an additional spring mounted in series with the main one. It's a setup borrowed directly from the 296 Challenge Evo. The semi-active dampers also get two additional rebound settings, allowing Ferrari to retain at least some compliance when driving on public roads.
The car rides on Pirelli P Zero R tires, with semi-slick P Zero Trofeo RS tires available as an option. Both were specifically developed for the car.
With no regenerative braking system to rely on, stopping power comes entirely from the carbon-ceramic brakes. The front discs measure 15.7 x 1.5 inches, while the rear ones measure 15 x 1.3 inches. Ferrari says the car can stop from 124 mph in just 331 feet.
The traction control system is predictive and calibrated specifically for track driving, marking a first for a road-going Ferrari. It's all managed by the FIVE system, derived from the one used in the F80.
The headline aerodynamic figure is 1,360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph, a 72 percent increase over the 296 GTB. Ferrari achieves this through several carefully designed elements:
- Front splitter: Extended and widened to generate more downforce.
- Front bumper: Curved aerodynamic flicks help manage airflow.
- Underbody: A fully enclosed floor and vortex generators improve aerodynamic efficiency.
- Aero dampers: Two ducts connect the underbody to the upper section of the car, helping keep downforce consistent when the nose dives under braking.
At the rear, a fixed wing derived from the 296 Challenge Evo generates 595 pounds of downforce on its own. There's one notable difference, though. Unlike the race car, the wing doesn't use a swan-neck mounting design. Instead, its supports attach from underneath to meet road homologation requirements, particularly those in the United States.
Ferrari's Centro Stile, led by Flavio Manzoni, took the clean design of the 296 and gave it a much more aggressive makeover. A technical insert on the hood, a wing suspended between two bumper-mounted "claws" inspired by the Evo, black metal mesh at the rear, and a double-keel diffuser all serve the same purpose. Here, form follows function.
Buyers looking to make their cars stand out can choose from a dedicated livery, three matte-finish wheel options, and even colored tire inserts through Pirelli's Color Edition program.
The Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale starts at approximately $307,000.

item.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix Delivers 50 Laps of Close Battles While Verstappen Holds On to Win
item.text:
Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.
Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.
At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.
On the second lap of the race, Russell, in a much faster Mercedes, passed Verstappen in the final corners coming off the Las Vegas Strip straight, then lost the lead before the first corner of the next lap. He would repeat this multiple times throughout the first half of the Grand Prix.
The race recorded a record 35 lead changes, but no one could cement a run past Verstappen.
With Verstappen slowing the field behind him, the first 10 laps of the race found the top three within one second and the top ten within less than 4.5 seconds.
On lap 20, Sergio Perez tried to make a pick on Rafeal Camera and the Haas, and Cadillac ended up tangled in the barrier, bringing out a full safety car. In a normal race, this would’ve neutralized the race, but with everyone still running bunched up, it just sent the field all together to the pits, leading to teams double-stacking against each other.
Hamilton was the biggest loser at the pit stop, having to serve a 10-second penalty that was not yet shared with him for a battle with Norris that he thought was just.
Hamilton was kept out while everyone else pitted to clear space for Charles Leclerc and was told about his penalty.
“Ah, that’s shit. If I turned in, we would’ve crashed.”
Under the safety car, Arvid Lindblad spun on cold tires to end his campaign for his first-ever podium. Arvid had his best starting spot of fifth for the Grand Prix and ran as high as third, while the Red Bulls on his sister team ran 1-2; he fell out of the points with the mistake.
Shortly after racing resumed, Isack Hadjar, who challenged his teammate Verstappen for the lead in the first half of the race and often put in the hardest position between the leader and the charging field, hit debris on the track and damaged his front wing. Hadjar pitted and finished outside the points as well.
With Red Bull and VCARB drivers out of contention, the door reopened for the Mercedes as Kimi Antonelli made his way into the picture following his grid drop, and Russell never left.
With two laps to go, Antonelli led Russell as the teammate fought for second; in turn 5, Russell went for the pass, overcommitted, and slid into the barrier.
Verstappen laughed on from ahead following a weekend of tension between the front-row starters.
Antonelli fell away from the lead battle on the penultimate lap with an internal issue and would come home fourth.
In the mayhem, the McLarens saw their luck change at Las Vegas. Following this double disqualification while battling for the championship last year, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri walked away with a shocking first double podium of the season.
“I led for about 15 seconds, so I’m very proud,” Norris joked.
Antonelli was followed by Pierre Gasly, Franco Colapinto, Lewis Hamilton, Carlos Sainz, George Russell and Charles Leclerc in the points-paying positions.
Victoria Beaver is a nomadic sports writer who spends her time hopping between race tracks and hippie farms. She’s covered every corner of motorsports that will let her in from 410 Sprints to NASCAR to Supercross. Her daily driver is a 2010 Subaru that she refused to do the smallest amount of preventative maintenance on. Instead, she spends her free time and money building a 42-foot Skoolie to one day travel the country full time.

item.title: Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale Is the Purest Prancing Horse in Years
item.text:
- Like its 360 Challenge Stradale predecessor, the 296 CS is a track-focused road car that shares more with the new 296 Challenge Evo race car than it does with the Ferrari 296GTB.
- Ditching the standard 296GTB's hybrid system, the 296 CS's twin-turbo V-6 makes 670 horsepower.
- The 296 Challenge Stradale is expected to go on sale in the U.S. in the third quarter of 2027, with a price of around $320,000.
Nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello. A few months ago, Ferrari unveiled the 12Cilindri Manuale, reintroducing a (simulated) six-speed manual transmission to its model lineup purely for the sake of driver involvement. And now, the Challenge Stradale badge returns to the rear engine mesh of a Prancing Horse for the first time since the 360 CS was discontinued in 2004. Simply put, it's a good year to be a sentimental Ferrarista.
In the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year. Parked side by side at their reveal at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya today, we would excuse a gentleman driver for confusing the CS with his new track-only machinery.

There have been several limited-edition, track-focused mid-engine Ferraris since the 360 Challenge Stradale—including the F430 Scuderia, 458 Speciale, and 488 Pista—but the 296 Challenge Stradale goes the furthest of all of them in emulating its racecar counterpart, both aesthetically and mechanically.
While previous track-centric Ferraris have been somewhat demurely styled, the 296 CS puts its aerodynamic elements on full display. The carbon-fiber rear wing, dive planes, adjustable front splitter, and vented hood are essentially a copy-paste job from the Challenge Evo, with concessions made for road legality. Up front, twin vents positioned in the hood just before the windshield channel hot air expelled from two under-hood radiators over the windshield and towards the rear of the car, reducing the aerodynamic variations caused by changing ground clearance.
Other aero features are hidden out of sight. The CS's underbody has been smoothed to better feed the rear diffuser and work with three pairs of vortex generators at the front and two at the rear to generate additional downforce. With all of the aerodynamic elements colluding, the 296 Challenge Stradale makes 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph. That's a 72-percent increase over the base 296GTB's peak figure.
Big changes have been made to the CS's powertrain. You won't find any orange high-voltage wiring snaking around under the glass of its mid-mounted hood like you would in a 296GTB or 296 Speciale, as the 5-kWh battery pack and rear-mounted axial-flux electric motor have been removed entirely. The twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 operates unassisted and supposedly sounds better than ever courtesy of a reworked twin-exit exhaust system.

Overall firepower has decreased to 670 horsepower—149 ponies less than the standard 296GTB's. The upside is a notable decrease in mass, with Ferrari claiming that the removal of the plug-in-hybrid componentry played a major role in shedding 328 pounds from the 296GTB's dry weight. A lightened transmission flex plate, driveshaft, and timing cover were also developed to make the CS's powertrain as featherweight as possible. Without an electric motor present to fill in any thrust gaps left by turbo lag, the V-6 has been retuned to increase low-end grunt, although peak torque remains 546 pound-feet delivered at 8250 rpm.
As to be expected, yanking out an integrated powertrain system comes with some unique challenges that affect more than just the engine itself. For example, Ferrari was forced to enlarge the 296 CS's rear carbon-ceramic brake discs and the ventilation ducts that cool them to compensate for the lack of regenerative braking. The decreased weight in the rear also shifted its weight distribution 1.5 percent to the front, which was addressed with suspension design and geometry changes.
The CS's newly developed suspension is derived directly from the 296 Challenge Evo and features semi-active dampers and a dual-spring design that improves rebound response. The result is reduced body roll, which helps the performance of the specially developed Pirelli P Zero R tires, measuring 245/35R20 in the front and 305/35R20 in the rear. The 20-inch forged wheels can be ordered in Matte Grigio Corsa, Matte Nero with a diamond-cut finish, or Matte Bianco Fuji.
The 296 Challenge Stradale's cockpit is very similar to the one found in the 296 Speciale. While niceties like climate control and a stereo remain, carbon-fiber door panels and a lack of armrests and storage pockets are a clear indication of the CS's weight-saving mission. For true gluttons for punishment, an even further stripped interior spec is available that removes the trim from the area beneath the seats and the lower section of the carpets beneath the center console, leaving part of the chassis exposed.
Ferrari is adamant that the 296 CS isn't a replacement for the 296 Speciale and will not cannibalize that model's customer base, as the two are intended for different buyers. Besides being geared less towards outright track duty, the 296 Speciale is a part of Ferrari's special series, meaning that customers need to have an "existing relationship" with the brand in order to get an allocation. The 296 Challenge Stradale is a standard range model, meaning anyone can walk into a dealer and order one, existing relationship or not. Ferrari says that it wants to court new Ferrari buyers interested in experiencing the purest driving experience that the prancing horse has to offer, and the 296 CS is the first step in that direction.
U.S. pricing has not been announced, but in its home market, the 296 Challenge Stradale costs 291,000 euros, or the equivalent of about $320,000. Stateside deliveries of the new CS are expected to begin sometime in late 2027. As a non-Speciale model, CS production numbers aren’t limited, which presents a unique opportunity to buy a special new Ferrari without already owning one.

item.title: A used Skoda Karoq could be the ultimate family car for just £6000
item.text:
If you loved the Skoda Yeti you'll... like its successor, the Karoq.
It's not a car to set the heart aflutter like the Yeti did, but that model arrived with a fresh niche appeal. Clearly the folk at Skoda decided its replacement should sell in far greater numbers to customers who were more keen to blend in.
It was a smart move. Within two years of its launch in 2017, the Karoq was Skoda's best-selling model. Thanks to its success in the showrooms, there are now plenty for sale on the forecourts at prices ranging from around £6500 for early, high-mileage cars to £25,000 or so for delivery-mileage pre-reg examples. The sweet spot is £15,000, for which you get a compact family SUV that is nevertheless spacious, comfortable and full of practical touches. You could say the same about many family SUVs, of course, but the Karoq shines thanks to both the value it represents and the reassuring sense of Skoda quality that is now so well established in the minds of buyers.
The Karoq's petrol engines are all turbocharged, represented first by a three-cylinder 1.0-litre that produces 113bhp. It's a willing motor that's capable of serious mileage, but we'd plump for the more powerful but equally efficient 148bhp 1.5 TSI with cylinder deactivation. Third up is the 2.0-litre 187bhp engine, but it's thirsty (it's only available with on-demand four-wheel drive) and easily outshined by the 1.5, which is also available with four-wheel drive but as an option. Diesels are a choice of 113bhp 1.6 or two 2.0-litre units, one making 187bhp (it was dropped from the range in 2020) and the other with 148bhp. They are much less plentiful than the petrols and out of step with today's market, but if you have something to tow, the 187bhp motor (it's partnered with four-wheel drive) is worth a go for its useful 295lb ft.
Dual-clutch automatic gearboxes are available on most engines as an alternative to the regular six-speed manual. Handling-and steering-wise, the Karoq is outclassed by its close stablemate the Seat Ateca. Instead, the Skoda is engineered for the undemanding driver, being comfortable and secure-feeling on the move but easily discomfited when pushed too hard.

item.title: Arizona Police Caught A BMW M2 Doing 170 MPH. The Driver Had A Terrible Excuse
item.text:
Arizona Police Caught A BMW M2 Doing 170 MPH. The Driver Had A Terrible Excuse
The driver claimed he was taking the BMW M2 for one last spin before trading it in.
One BMW driver's final trip in his M2 didn't go quite as planned. Arizona State Police arrested the driver after allegedly catching him traveling at 170 mph on a busy highway, more than 100 mph over the posted speed limit.
His explanation? He was about to trade in the car and wanted one last drive.
The incident happened on November 9 along State Route 202 near Sky Harbor Boulevard in Tempe, Arizona. According to the Arizona Department of Public Safety (AZDPS), a highway patrol trooper spotted a gray 2023 BMW M2 passing other traffic at an extremely high rate of speed.
Using a LIDAR device, the trooper recorded the BMW traveling at 170 mph in a 65-mph zone. That's 105 mph over the posted limit, and fast enough to cover approximately 250 feet every second.
Rather than attempting to chase the BMW at that speed, the trooper coordinated with the Highway Patrol Traffic Operations Center to track the vehicle. Authorities eventually spotted the M2 cutting across multiple lanes of traffic to reach the McClintock Drive exit.
When the trooper caught up with the driver after the BMW left the highway, there was another problem: The car didn't have a license plate.
BMW M2
When questioned about his speed, the driver initially estimated that he had been traveling between 110 and 115 mph. He later told the trooper he hadn't realized just how fast he was going.
According to AZDPS, the driver also explained that he was planning to trade in the BMW and wanted to take it for one final drive before handing over the keys. That explanation didn't get him off the hook. Police arrested the driver on suspicion of reckless driving and endangerment. Authorities haven't publicly identified him.
Unsurprisingly, Arizona authorities weren't particularly impressed with the driver's farewell outing. In a social media post, AZDPS reminded motorists that speed limits exist to protect everyone on the road and encouraged drivers to save their need for speed for the track.
At 170 mph, there's very little room for error. A vehicle traveling that fast covers nearly the length of a football field every second. That's a lot of ground to cover before another driver even has time to react.

item.title: Ferrari Revives Challenge Stradale Name For A Hardcore, Non-Hybrid 296
item.text:
Ferrari Revives Challenge Stradale Name For A Hardcore, Non-Hybrid 296
Ferrari ditches the hybrid for the street-legal 296 Challenge Stradale, shedding weight and piling on downforce to create the ultimate track toy.
Ferrari has revived one of the coolest nameplates of its modern era, creating the wildest and most track-focused variant of its entry-level supercar yet. The new 296 Challenge Stradale is a roadgoing version of the updated 296 Challenge Evo racecar, adopting motorsport-inspired aero and chassis upgrades while ditching the plug-in hybrid system for pure V6 power.
The spiritual successor to the 360 Challenge Stradale from the '00s prioritizes mechanical simplicity, lightness, and handling prowess over outright power.
Starting with the exterior, the front end is distinguished by the pronounced splitter, the larger ducts on the hood, and the dual canards on the bumper. The tail has also been redesigned with a fixed rear wing, side fins, dual tailpipes, and a more complex diffuser with integrated spoilers.
According to Ferrari, the new aero components, the fully enclosed underbody and five pairs of vortex generators allow the 296 Challenge Stradale to produce 617 kg (1,360 lbs) of downforce at 250 kph (155 mph). This represents an increase of 72% compared to the 296 GTB, and 42% compared to the 296 Speciale.
The first non-electrified street-legal 296
The Challenge Stradale is the first roadgoing member of the 296 family with a non-hybrid powertrain, mirroring its track-only sibling. The electric motor and the high-voltage battery are gone, letting the twin-turbo 3.0-liter V6 do the work by itself. The dry-sump engine gains hardware from the Ferrari Challenge race program, generating 661 hp (493 kW / 670 PS) and 740 Nm (546 lb-ft) of torque. Power is routed to the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch F1 gearbox.
While it can't match the combined output of the plug-in hybrid 296 GTB (819 hp) and 296 Speciale (868 hp), the Challenge Stradale is faster than both of them around the track. More specifically, it laps Fiorano in 1'18”500, which is 2.5 seconds faster than the 296 GTB and 0.5 seconds faster than the 296 Speciale.
Besides the new aero, this is largely due to its 1.98 kg/PS power-to-weight ratio. By saying goodbye to electrification, the Challenge Stradale strikes a dry weight of 1,330 kg (2,932 lbs), which is 140 kg (309 lbs) less than the 296 GTB and 80 kg (176 lbs) lighter than the 296 Speciale. Removing the hybrid system was no easy task, as Ferrari had to engineer a mechanical A/C compressor, a Belt Starter Generator with alternator and starter functions, and a new driveline.
Of course, they didn't forget the sound, with a Challenge Stradale-specific exhaust and an optional non-homologated track-only exhaust system to rival the notoriously loud 360 Challenge Stradale.
Interior and chassis upgrades
The diet continues inside the cabin, with single-piece door panels and central console made of carbon fiber, and an optional set of carbon seats borrowed from the SF90 XX Stradale. There is also the option of an exposed-chassis interior trim that strips carpets and under-seat paneling. Still, the model retains amenities like wireless charging, ADAS, dual cameras, and Matrix LED headlights.
As for the chassis setup, the suspension comprises recalibrated semi-active dampers with nearly doubled spring rates, motorsport-derived helper springs, and bespoke Pirelli P Zero R or Trofeo RS tires. Ferrari claims that stability has improved by 34% compared to the 296 GTB, with a 68% reduction in the roll gradient.
In a similar context, the electronic suite has been revised for the best possible lap times. The model gets a new track-tuned predictive slip control system, an F80-derived Ferrari Integrated Vehicle Estimator (FIVE), and ABS Evo operating across all five Manettino modes. Beefier carbon ceramic brakes measuring 398 mm (15.7 in) up front and 380 mm (15 in) at the rear complete the revisions.
As for straight line performance, the Challenge Stradale matches the 0-100 kph (0-62 mph) acceleration of the Speciale at 2.8 seconds. However, it is a full 0.9 seconds slower in the 0-200 kph (0-124 mph) sprint, completing it in 7.9 seconds.
Ferrari didn't announce pricing for the Challenge Stradale, but Autocar reports it will cost around the same with the 296 GTB.
What about the 296 Challenge Evo race car?
The 296 Challenge Evo is the successor of the racing model originally introduced in 2023. It shares the non-hybrid twin-turbo V6 with its predecessor, producing 690 hp (515 kW / 700 PS) and 740 Nm (546 lb-ft) of torque, mated to a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox.
The biggest difference in the Evo is the redesigned aero. The team made changes to the front splitter, bumper, mirrors, underbody, adjustable rear wing and rear diffuser, allowing the racecar to produce 12% more maximum downforce compared to the outgoing 296 Challenge. There is also the option of increasing rear ride height by up to 10 mm (0.4 in) for a further boost in downforce. In the opposite direction, teams have access to a Low Drag kit for faster tracks, which cuts drag by 4% by removing two flicks from the bumper and one nolder from the wheel arch.
The Challenge Evo rides on 19-inch wheels shod in slick tires, and has larger brakes compared to its roadgoing counterpart. Furthermore, it has a stripped out cabin with a roll cage, a racing bucket, a removable F1-style steering wheel, custom switches on the center console, and an optional passenger seat for coaching.
According to Ferrari, the 296 Challenge Evo is 0.8 seconds faster than its predecessor at the Mugello track. The new racecar will debut in the 2027 Ferrari Challenge Seasons in Europe and North America before expanding to regional series in 2028.

item.title: Chevrolet Corvette (C2)
item.text:
The Chevrolet Corvette (C2) is the second-generation Corvette sports car, produced by the Chevrolet division of General Motors (GM) for the 1963 through 1967 model years.


== History ==

After 10 years of tinkering with the basic C1 package, albeit much improved, Corvette's designers and engineers knew it was time to move on from Harley Earl's original C1 design.
C2 (Corvette 2nd generation) inspiration was drawn from several sources: 

GM's Q-Corvette exercise of 1957
GM's Corvette SS 1957 racing sports car
the radical Sting Ray Racer Mitchell designed in 1959
the contemporary Jaguar E-Type, one of which Mitchell owned and drove frequently
a Mako shark Mitchell caught while deep-sea fishing
CERV I concept of 1959

The Q-Corvette exercise of 1957 envisioned a smaller, more advanced Corvette as a coupe-only model, boasting a rear transaxle, independent rear suspension, and four-wheel disc brakes, with the rear brakes mounted inboard. Exterior styling was purposeful, with peaked fenders, a long nose, and a short, bobbed tail.
Meanwhile, Director of High-Performance Zora Arkus-Duntov and other GM engineers had become fascinated with mid and rear-engine designs. Duntov explored the mid/rear-engine layout with the lightweight, open-wheel, single-seat CERV I concept of 1959. 
A rear-engined Corvette was briefly considered during 1958–60, progressing as far as a full-scale mock-up designed around the Corvair's entire rear-mounted power package, including its air-cooled flat-six, as an alternative to the Corvette's usual water-cooled V8.
By the fall of 1959, elements of the Q-Corvette and the Sting Ray Special racer would be incorporated into experimental project XP-720, which sought to deliver improved passenger accommodation, more luggage space, and superior ride and handling over previous Corvettes, and led directly to the C2 design.


== Development ==
For the first time in the Corvette's history, wind tunnel testing influenced the final shape, as did practical matters like interior space, windshield curvatures, and tooling limitations. Both body styles were extensively evaluated as production-ready 3/8-scale models at the Caltech wind tunnel.
The vehicle's inner structure received as much attention as the aerodynamics of its exterior. Fiberglass outer panels were retained, but the Sting Ray emerged with nearly twice as much steel support in its central structure as the 1958–62 Corvette. The resulting extra weight was balanced by a reduction in fiberglass thickness, so the finished product actually weighed a bit less than the old roadster. Passenger room was as good as before despite the tighter wheelbase, and the reinforcing steel girder made the cockpit both stronger and safer.
The C2 program was directed by Ed Cole, Duntov, and GM chief stylist Bill Mitchell, who dubbed the model "Sting Ray" (after the earlier race car of the same name). Styling was led by Larry Shinoda; Pete Brock was also instrumental.


=== Styling & design ===

While Duntov was developing an innovative new chassis for the 1963 Corvette, designers were adapting and refining the basic look of the racing Sting Ray for the production model. A fully functional space buck (a wooden mock-up created to work out interior dimensions) was completed by early 1960, production coupe styling was locked up for the most part by April, and the interior, instrument panel included, was in place by November. Only in the fall of 1960 did the designers turn their creative attention to a new version of the traditional Corvette convertible and, still later, its detachable hardtop.
The first-ever production Corvette coupe sported a fastback body with a long hood and a raised windsplit that ran the length of the roof and continued down the back on a pillar that bisected the rear window into right and left halves. The split backlite is usually attributed to Mitchell, who claimed to have been inspired by the 57SC  Bugatti "Atlantique" coupe. The feature actually predated both the C2 Corvette and Bob McLean's Q-Corvette, having been used by Harley Earl on both his Oldsmobile Golden Rocket show car and his own more traditional design studies for the C2 Corvette, some of which had progressed to full-scale models. Earl's inspiration was said to have been a Scaglione-bodied Alfa Romeo coupé shown at the 1954 Turin Auto Show. A similar design would be used by the third-generation Buick Riviera that ran from 1971 to 1973.
Quad headlamps were retained but newly hidden – the first American car so equipped since the 1942 DeSoto. The lamps were mounted in rotating housings that blended with the sharp-edged front end when "closed". Hidden headlamps would be a feature of the Corvette until the C6 model debuted in 2005. Coupe doors were cut into the roof, which made entry/exit easier in such a low-slung closed car. Faux vents were located in the hood and on the coupe's rear pillars; functional ones had been intended but were cancelled due to cost considerations.

The Sting Ray's interior carried a re-interpretation of the twin-cowl Corvette dash motif used since 1958, but a more practical one incorporating a roomy glovebox, an improved heater, and the cowl-ventilation system. A full set of round gauges included a huge speedometer and tachometer. The control tower center console returned, somewhat slimmer but now containing the clock and a vertically situated radio.
Luggage space was improved as well, although due to the lack of an external trunklid, cargo had to be loaded behind the seats. The large round deck emblem was newly hinged to double as a fuel-filler flap, replacing the previous left-flank door.


=== Engineering ===
Though not as obvious as the car's radical styling, the new chassis was just as important to the Sting Ray's success. Maneuverability was improved thanks to the faster recirculating ball, or "Ball-Race", steering, and a shorter wheelbase. The latter might ordinarily imply a choppier ride, but the altered weight distribution partly compensated for it. Less weight on the front wheels also meant easier steering, and with some 80 additional pounds on the rear wheels, the Sting Ray offered improved traction. Stopping power improved, too. Four-wheel cast-iron 11-inch drum brakes remained standard but were now wider, for an increase in effective braking area. Sintered-metallic linings, segmented for cooling, were again optional. So were Al-Fin brake drums, which not only provided faster heat dissipation (and thus better fade resistance) but less unsprung weight. Power assist was available with both brake packages.

The independent rear suspension created by Duntov was derived from the CERV I concept, and included a frame-mounted differential with U-jointed half-shafts tied together by a transverse leaf spring. Rubber-cushioned struts carried the differential, which reduced ride harshness while improving tire adhesion, especially on rougher roads. item.text: Ferrari built just 10 NART Spiders, and only one of them went to movie star, car guy, and “King of Cool” Steve McQueen. That car just sold for $18,925,000 (including buyer’s premium) at an auction in New York City. Is that a lot of money? Of course. But, given the car that money bought and who the car’s first owner was, you could also answer that question, “Not really.” Gooding Christie's Ferrari started building its 275 GTB in 1964. Bodied by Scaglietti and powered by a 3.3-liter version of the Colombo V-12 engine mated to a five-speed transaxle, the model lasted until 1968. It was built in both short- and long-nose body styles, could be had with all-aluminum bodywork, and came with both two- and four-cam versions, but Ferrari made no plans to offer anything but a coupe. The mechanically similar drop-top 275 GTS had completely different, more conservative styling. Enter Luigi Chinetti, the New York–based racer, owner of the North American Racing Team (NART), and Ferrari distributor. Knowing that his American customers enjoyed some sun on their faces and wind in their hair, he had helped convince Ferrari to build the California Spider on the 250 platform in the late ’50s, and he saw a similar opportunity with the 275 GTB, especially when the four-cam version debuted in late 1966. At Chinetti’s urging, a small batch of GTB/4s left Scaglietti sans roof. Chinetti sold them through his dealership, fitted with a not-so-subtle NART badge on the tail. “ NART Spider ” was never an official designation, but the name stuck. Gooding Christie's Gooding Christie's While Chinetti thought he could sell 25 examples, only 10 were completed. The first chassis finished second in class at Sebring in 1967, got a repaint, and made the cover of Road & Track . The magazine called it “the most satisfying sports car in the world.” Another NART Spider appeared in the 1968 film The Thomas Crown Affair , starring Steve McQueen. The “red Italian thing” doesn’t get a ton of screen time, but it must have made an impression on the actor, because he went right out and bought this one—chassis 10453. The sixth NART Spider built, it crossed the Atlantic in the fall of ’67 finished in Blu Sera over black Connolly leather. McQueen, who personalized many of his cars to at least some degree, apparently didn’t like the color and had it repainted in a different shade of metallic blue. He also had the bumpers removed and an external quick-fill fuel cap installed, along with a smaller, rally-style mirror. The seats were also retrimmed with a different stitch pattern. According to Gooding Christie’s, not long into McQueen’s ownership a truck hit the NART Spider from behind on the Pacific Coast Highway and pushed it into the car ahead, causing damage at both ends of that glorious Scaglietti shape. The car was soon repaired and repainted in the same metallic blue, modified with flared fenders and a flip-tail rear. Gooding also notes that the “surviving record does not establish how often McQueen drove his NART Spider or exactly when it left his possession, and no period photographs are known to show him with it.” McQueen didn’t keep it too long, as it was with another California owner by 1971. The current owner bought it from a Long Island Ferrari dealer in 1985, and it has remained in largely preserved condition ever since. Gooding Christie's This was the star car of Gooding Christie’s NYC auction this week, coinciding with the inaugural Retromobile New York, a classic car expo similar to the long-running Rétromobile Paris. Bidding opened at $10M and slowly worked its way to the $17.2M hammer price, which falls right within Gooding’s presale estimate range of $15M–$20M. The $18.9M final price makes it, by our count, the 31st most expensive car ever sold at auction. A car as rare and sought after as the NART Spider tends to stay in long-term collector ownership, and public sales almost never happen. Another one did come to market in 2013, though, and it sold for the much higher sum of $27,500,000 . Unlike the blue car sold this week, it was a one-owner car with no accident history or modifications, and it boasted a full restoration. It would have been reasonable to think that the blue car would’ve been able to make up for it with the Steve McQueen history. After all, multiple ex-McQueen cars and motorcycles have come to auction over the years, and they tend to bring a big premium . One recent and fairly direct comparable is his 275 GTB coupe that sold in 2023 for $5.4M , nearly $2M more than the model’s condition #1 (concours) value in our price guide at the time. That said, the market for vintage Ferraris has been on the soft side this year, even as more modern Ferraris smash records and make headlines. It’s also possible that McQueen’s star is fading a bit. He died 46 years ago, and his biggest car film, Le Mans , came out 55 years ago. But regardless of Enzo-era Ferrari pricing or whether someone can be the King of Cool forever, this is one of the most important and expensive cars sold anywhere this year. item.title: Honda, Toyota Recalling 1.6 Million More Vehicles Over Takata Airbags
item.text:
18 years after Honda filed the first official airbag recall and 12 years since the first round of mass recalls began, the Takata airbag scandal remains ongoing. This month, Honda and Toyota have both filed new recalls with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration related to faulty airbag inflators.
The pair of recalls filed in November include a population of more than 1.6 million vehicles. Late-model Hondas make up over 810,000 units in the recall, while Toyota accounts for 790,000 units, 314,000 of which are located in the United States. NHTSA documents indicate that 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX, 2013 Acura RDX models, 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 ‌IS250, 2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner models are included in the recall.
Despite the growing recall population, the core issue remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls. “The airbag inflator propellant can degrade with repeated exposure to high-humidity environments and large temperature variation, resulting in increased internal pressure. If an affected airbag deploys, the increased internal pressure may cause the inflator to rupture (break apart) and deploy abnormally,” NHTSA documents explain. “In the event of an inflator rupture, metal fragments could pass through the airbag cushion material possibly causing serious injury or fatality to vehicle occupants.”
There have been no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being newly recalled. However, NHTSA has recorded 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009. The Takata airbag recall remains the largest recall in U.S. history.
Given the rolling nature of the Takata recall, Honda and Toyota were already in discussions with federal regulators when this airbag version began to show signs of degradation. Honda first identified an issue during simulation testing under severe environmental conditions in May 2025. However, these tests didn’t show abnormal inflator behavior or a “statistically significant deviation” from previous prediction models. Similarly, Toyota had been collecting and studying certain Takata inflators since 2016, specifically focusing on a desiccated, phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate (PSAN) propellant. Toyota’s predictive models indicated that some of these inflators could be reaching the end of their life, prompting the Japanese automaker to conduct a voluntary safety recall.
The remedy is fairly simple for both automakers: Toyota and Honda will simply replace the airbag inflators on affected units. Honda says its new inflators are manufactured by a different supplier and use a different propellant that does not degrade over the long term when exposed to high temperatures, high humidity, and large temperature fluctuations. Either way, both automakers and federal regulators urge affected owners to have their airbag inflators swapped out as soon as possible.

item.title: Court Bars BYD Ti7 From Sale In Europe For Looking Way Too Much Like A Land Rover Defender
item.text:
Court Bars BYD Ti7 From Sale In Europe For Looking Way Too Much Like A Land Rover Defender
China's BYD is now officially barred from selling its Ti7 SUV in Europe because a Dutch district court in The Hague ruled that it looked far too much like the Land Rover Defender. While it's certainly not a one-to-one copy, I can certainly see why the folks over at Jaguar-Land Rover's legal department would be a bit miffed.
Although it has been on sale in China since last year, JLR launched the case earlier this year after BYD announced on its UK website that the seven-seater would be available to order, with customer deliveries starting in January of 2027, according to Reuters. Now, there's an injunction against its sale in the EU. The one caveat of all of this is that this court in the Netherlands has no jurisdiction over BYD's affiliate in the UK.
The injunction against BYD will take effect a week after the ruling since the automaker "currently has no concrete plans to place the Ti7 on the market in the EU," according to Reuters. Until the whole intellectual property case is resolved, the court is banning BYD from producing the — admittedly good-looking — vehicle at its new factory in Hungary. It's due to spin up mass production of other vehicles next year, but the Ti7 will not be one of them unless something drastic changes very quickly.
"In these summary proceedings, the preliminary relief judge rules that the Ti7 infringes the EU design of Jaguar Land Rover," Reuters reports the court ruling said. "The characteristic and distinctive elements of the design are reflected in the BYD Ti7."
The knockoff
Some of the more notable visual similarities are the boxy, flat-roof silhouette, its upright proportions, its side-hinged tailgate and squared-off wheel arches. The real kicker has to be the solid body-colored panel behind the rear passenger door, which is controversial on the Defender, yet BYD designers decided to include it anyway.
It's actually fairly rare in Europe for a large automaker to go to court over design rights infringement. It's also uncommon for a ruling to come down so early in proceedings for a case that is ongoing and likely to last some time. JLR, of course, is pleased with the outcome, telling Reuters, "We protect our intellectual property and take legal action when necessary."
Still, this isn't exactly the first time something like this has happened, as Reuters explains:
Legacy automakers have often complained that Chinese automakers have copied designs, though little has been proven in court. In 2005, for instance, General Motors and Chinese rival Chery settled a case over the Chery QQ that the No. 1 US automaker said was a copy of its Chevrolet Spark.
BYD, for its part, "strongly disagrees" with The Hauge's ruling and is planning to appeal, telling the Wall Street Journal that the Ti7 is "the result of BYD's own independent design work and infringes none of JLR's rights." It added that it will "pursue every legal avenue to demonstrate that this decision is incorrect."
